questions.q: What does `az account set --subscription "Contoso-Production"` actually do?
options: Lists every subscription available to the signed-in account
Creates a brand-new subscription named Contoso-Production
Switches which subscription subsequent az commands target, until it's changed again
Permanently deletes every other subscription on the account
questions.explain: az account set changes the active subscription; every command run afterward targets that subscription until you switch again.

questions.q: What is the general shape every Azure CLI command follows?
options: az <group> <command> --<parameter> <value>
There is no consistent shape to Azure CLI commands
azure <parameter> --<group> <command>
<command> az --group <value>
questions.explain: The CLI is organized into command groups by service area (vm, group, storage, network), each followed by a command and its parameters.

questions.q: Why would a script use `az vm list --output tsv` instead of `--output table`?
options: table output runs faster than tsv output
Scripts cannot parse table output under any circumstances
tsv is the only format that returns real data; table output is fake
tsv is tab-separated with no headers, which is easy to loop over in a shell script
questions.explain: tsv's plain tab-separated rows, without the decorative borders and headers of table output, are what a script loops over cleanly.

questions.q: What does `--query` do that `--output` does not?
options: It selects and reshapes which data comes back, using a JMESPath expression on the raw JSON
It deletes any resource that doesn't match the filter
It formats the already-selected data for on-screen display
It changes which subscription the command runs against
questions.explain: --query filters/reshapes the underlying JSON with JMESPath before --output decides how that result is displayed.

questions.q: In `--query "[].{Name:name, Size:hardwareProfile.vmSize}"`, what does the leading `[]` mean?
options: Reverse the order of the returned list
Return an empty result unless a filter is added
Return only the first item in the list
Apply the expression to every item in the returned list
questions.explain: [] in JMESPath means "for every element in this array," so the {Name:..., Size:...} object is built once per VM in the list.
